trigger_or_context: Something bothers you or you two do not agree. A hard talk could happen.
short_term_function: Staying quiet keeps things calm right now and stops the hard talk from happening.
developmental_cost: The problem never gets worked out. The other person may not know something is wrong.
adaptive_alternative_1: When something bothers you, pick a calm moment. Name one thing you saw and one thing you need.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if the two of you can work through hard things together.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: The talk may feel uncomfortable. They may not take it well.
context_conditions: If speaking up is not safe, like if the other person gets mean or scary, your safety comes first.
review_reason: Safety context — avoiding conflict can be protective when the other person is unsafe.

trigger_or_context: A problem needs to be named. You notice you are the one who always brings it up.
short_term_function: Bringing things up gets the problem named instead of letting it sit.
developmental_cost: You carry all the work of raising hard things. You cannot tell if they would ever start one.
adaptive_alternative_1: If you keep being the only one who brings things up, say that out loud. Then leave room to see if they start too.
what_new_response_supports: You see if the work of raising hard things can be shared, or stays only on you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: They may not step up. You sit with not raising every little thing yourself.
context_conditions: Bringing things up is healthy. This is about the balance, not about going silent.
review_reason: Meaning depends on the balance of who raises issues; function is partly inferred.

trigger_or_context: You have raised something before. Nothing shifted, so you go quiet.
short_term_function: Going quiet saves your effort when talking has not led to any change.
developmental_cost: The other person stops hearing what is wrong. Nothing can shift because it is no longer named.
adaptive_alternative_1: Instead of going quiet, name the pattern. Say you have raised this before and nothing changed, and ask what would need to shift.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if real change is possible here, or not.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: They may still not change. You may have to face what that means.
context_conditions: If you have truly named it many times and nothing changes, going quiet may be part of deciding, not just giving up.
review_reason: Can shade toward discernment after repeated genuine attempts; context-sensitive.

trigger_or_context: A hard conversation is needed. It feels tiring, so you skip it.
short_term_function: Skipping the talk saves your energy and spares you the tiring conversation right now.
developmental_cost: Hard things stay unsolved. The other person may not know it matters to you.
adaptive_alternative_1: Pick one hard thing and a calm time. Keep it short: say what is wrong and one thing you need.
what_new_response_supports: You learn if hard talks can be shorter and go somewhere, instead of always draining you.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Starting the talk takes energy. It may still feel hard.
context_conditions: If the talk is tiring because the other person is mean or scary, your safety comes first.
review_reason: Safety context — avoidance can be protective when the other person is unsafe.
